assetCapital.asset: Flight fuelling turnaround and delay exposure
assetCapital.basis: 0.12% of flight fuelling turnaround delay exposure avoided through automated meter-to-loadsheet density reconciliation and zero-drag paperwork closeout
assetCapital.source: ~120 aviation fuel stations refuelling ~2,500 flights per day (~900,000 flights/yr). Commercial airline ground delays carry benchmark direct operating costs of $65-$100+ per minute (~₹5,500-₹8,500/min). Under airline into-plane service level agreements (SLAs) and IATA model fuel supply agreements, fuelling-attributable delays exceeding scheduled turnaround buffers trigger SLA penalty chargebacks and handler dispute costs averaging ~₹35,000 per incident. Automated volume-to-mass conversion (Agent 6) and digital batch release (Agent 1) eliminate ~1,080 delayed fuelling handoffs annually (~₹3.78 Cr/yr).

assetRisk.scenario: Contaminated or off-spec aviation turbine fuel uplift requiring emergency aircraft defuelling, tank flushing, and flight cancellation
assetRisk.source: ~120 aviation fuel stations (AFS) across the national network. Baseline frequency of 0.05 events per station-year reflects ~1 off-spec fuel delivery incident every 20 station-years (~6 events/yr across ~900,000 annual fuelling uplifts, or ~6.7 per million operations). Consequence of ₹4.5 Cr (~US$540k) covers emergency airside defuelling, downgrading/disposal of contaminated Jet A-1, aircraft fuel manifold flushing and filter replacements, passenger compensation / flight rebooking, and airline SLA penalty chargebacks under IATA model agreements. Alpha (0.35) reflects the causal share attributable to informational and verification errors (missed CoA limits, uncorrected filter dP drops, misread chemical water detector capsules, or uncertified tank lineup); beta (0.40) reflects the agent squad's verified efficacy across continuous CoA auditing (Agent 1), flow-corrected dP trending (Agent 2), and digital water detection verification (Agent 5).

rationale: P55 Aviation Fuelling Supervisor governs fuel quality, airport depot bulk storage, hydrant pumping loops, and into-plane fuelling operations across ~120 Aviation Fuel Stations (AFS) supplying ~2,500 commercial, cargo, and defense flights daily (~900,000 flights/yr). Headcount of 200 seats (~0.65% of enterprise staff, ~4.4% of downstream technical population) provides defensible 24/7/365 coverage: ~50 seats across 10-12 high-tempo major metro hubs (4-5 shift supervisors per hub on rotating shifts), ~75 seats across ~35 tier-2 commercial airport AFS (2-3 supervisors per airport), ~60 seats across ~73 regional, UDAN, and remote/defense airfields (averaging ~0.82 per station with regional relief pooling), and ~15 seats in central and regional aviation quality compliance cells (governing JIG 1/2, EI 1530, and civil aviation standards). Asset Capital is formulated in volume form across 900,000 annual flight fuelling turnarounds, recovering 0.12% (12 bps) of flight delay exposure (~₹3.78 Cr/yr) through automated temperature-density conversions, prover meter factor reconciliation, and instant digital loadsheet closeout (Agent 6), eliminating turnaround bottlenecks without encroaching on airline fleet ownership. Asset Risk targets contaminated or off-spec fuel uplifts requiring emergency aircraft defuelling, fuel downgrading, and grounding across 120 AFS (frequency 0.05/yr, consequence ₹4.5 Cr, alpha*beta = 0.14, avoiding ₹3.78 Cr/yr in expected losses). Resource Recovery is strictly null as downstream aviation fuel distribution does not discover or book subsurface hydrocarbons, complying with the portfolio rule prohibiting joint Integrity and Recovery claims.
caveats: 1. If an operator takes the strictest view of value_model.js that assetCapital must be restricted exclusively to the refiner-marketer's owned balance-sheet physical assets (analogous to P19 Process Safety and P30 Inspection), assetCapital can be set to null without compromising model coherence, anchoring value in Human Capital (₹45.00 Cr/yr across 200 seats at 1,800 h/yr, 50% on-task, ₹2,500/h) and Asset Risk (₹3.78 Cr/yr). 2. If an operator alternatively prefers an infrastructure-based time-form parameterization for assetCapital, the equivalent defensible shape is: {form: 'time', asset: 'Aviation Fuel Station (AFS) into-plane fuelling systems', units: 120, unitLabel: 'aviation fuel stations', hoursPerYear: 8760, share: 0.001, ratePerHour: 40000, basis: '0.10% of station operating availability recovered by eliminating filter blinding throttles, accelerating batch settling releases, and avoiding custody reconciliation hold-ups (~8.76 h/station/yr)', source: '~120 AFS; ₹40k/station-hour reflects throughput capacity and marketing margin; delivers ~₹4.20 Cr/yr'}. 3. If an operator prioritizes apron physical containment hazards over aircraft contamination, the equivalent Asset Risk scenario is apron hydrant surge rupture or EFSO failure: {unitsPerYear: 120, unitLabel: 'aviation fuel stations', frequency: 0.015, consequence: 150000000, alpha: 0.30, beta: 0.35, expected loss avoided: ₹2.84 Cr/yr} covering pressurized apron jet fuel spills, emergency foam deployment, and concrete taxiway excavation. 4. All physical hydrant pit coupling, mobile bowser maneuvering, and manual emergency shutoff pushbuttons remain under human airside operator control.
